title: Quorum reads and writes: R + W > N
description: Any node can coordinate. Consistency is a per-operation dial rather than a property of the database: make the read set and the write set overlap and a read always sees the newest acknowledged write.

nodes.label: Coordinator
nodes.sublabel: any node can take this role

nodes.label: R + W > N
nodes.sublabel:
N=3, W=2, R=2 → the read and
write sets must share at least
one replica, so a read cannot

Tolerates one node down.

steps.text: The client sends a put to whichever node it reached. That node becomes the coordinator for this operation — there is no special primary to fail over.
The coordinator sends the write to all three replicas in parallel.
It waits for W = 2 acknowledgements, then confirms to the client. The third replica may still be writing, or may be down — the write is already durable on a majority either way.
Latency is set by the second-fastest replica, not the slowest. That is why quorum writes stay fast even with a straggler in the set.
The client sends a get. The coordinator must decide how many replicas to consult.
It reads from R = 2 — replicas A and B. Because 2 + 2 > 3, the read set and the last write set must share at least one replica, so the newest acknowledged value is among these responses.

Suppose B returns an older version than A. The coordinator compares versions, returns A's value to the client, and writes the newer value back to B in the background. That is read repair — and note it applies to a replica that was actually read, not to the one left out.

Replica C was never consulted, so this read did nothing to fix it. Keys that are rarely read are repaired instead by anti-entropy: replicas periodically exchange Merkle trees and reconcile only the ranges whose hashes differ.
W = 1, R = 1: fastest on both paths and only eventually consistent, because the read set and write set need not overlap. Fine for a profile view; wrong for an account balance.
W = 3: strongly consistent for reads at R = 1, but a single unavailable replica blocks every write. Availability and consistency, traded explicitly.
W = 2, R = 2 is the usual default: strongly consistent, and it survives one node being down on either path. The point is that this is chosen per operation, not per database.
